title: st.data_editor NumberColumn: typing a value starting with "." (no leading zero) drops the decimal point and reads digits as a whole number
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a NumberColumn cell is selected and you type a value that starts with `.` (e.g. `.01`), the `.` is silently dropped and the remaining digits are committed as a whole number — `.01` becomes `1`, `.07` becomes `7`. Typing the same value with a leading zero (`0.01`) works correctly, and **pasting** `.01` into the cell also works correctly. So this is specific to the character-by-character typed-entry path.

Impact
This is a real-world data-entry trap: any user in the habit of typing .01-style shorthand (common for percentage/margin fields) silently enters a value the cell just shows a plausible-looking wrong number.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
df = pd.DataFrame({"Customer": ["A", "B"], "Margin": [12.0, 8.0]})
st.data_editor(
    df,
    column_config={
        "Margin": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Margin", format="%.4f", step=0.0001),
    },
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Click the Margin cell for row A (shows 12.0000).
Type .07 (as literal keystrokes: ., 0, 7).
Press Enter.



### Expected Behavior

Expected: cell shows 0.0700.


### Current Behavior

Actual: cell shows 7.0000.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

Streamlit version: 1.61.1
Python version: 3.12/3.14
Browser: Chrome
OS: Windows


### Additional Information

_No response_

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16909)

This is a frontend bug in `st.data_editor` `NumberColumn`: typing a value that starts with `.` (e.g. `.07`) silently drops the decimal, so the remaining digits commit as an integer (`7.0000` instead of `0.0700`). Pasting `.01` and typing `0.01` both work, which matches the two different input paths. Streamlit’s own parsers are not the problem — `toSafeNumber` / `NumberColumn.getCell` already accept leading-dot strings such as `".1312314"` (covered by unit tests), and paste goes through `getCell` with the full string. Typed entry instead uses Glide Data Grid’s built-in `GridCellKind.Number` overlay (`react-number-format`), which Streamlit does not replace (`useCustomEditors` returns `undefined` for number cells). That overlay is a controlled numeric input that reports a JS `floatValue` on every keystroke; a lone `.` is not a valid number, so the decimal is discarded and later digits are read as a whole number. A fix would keep the in-progress text (similar to `st.number_input`’s `formattedValue`) or patch the overlay so incomplete input like `.` / `.0` is preserved.

### Related Issues

- [#16129](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16129) — Same Glide `NumberColumn` overlay editor; IME composition committed after the first keystroke. Streamlit already patches that overlay for #16129, so this is another overlay typing-path bug rather than a `getCell` parsing issue.
- [#12886](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12886) — Similar “decimal disappears while typing” symptom in `st.number_input` (`1.0` collapsing to `1`). Related UX, but a different widget and input implementation; not a duplicate.
- [#11519](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11519) — Another `NumberColumn` editing-path numeric distortion (`4.52` rounding to `4.51` with `step`/`format`). Same feature area, different failure mode.

No exact duplicate of the leading-`.` typed-entry case was found.
